title: First, Not Only
scripture_text: But seek first God's Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
body:
Jesus had just spent several minutes talking about clothes and food and birds. It is a surprisingly ordinary passage. He is not telling worried people to care about nothing; He is telling them He knows exactly what they are worried about, down to the grocery list.

And then: seek first. Not seek only. Following Jesus does not mean your grades, your team, your job and your friendships stop mattering. It means they stop being first. There is only one first, and whatever occupies it quietly organizes everything else.

The test is not what you say matters most. The test is what your calendar and your attention already answer. Where does your mind go the second it is unoccupied? That is a more honest answer than anything you would write down.

Rearranging that order is not one dramatic decision. It is a hundred small ones — what you do with the first ten minutes of the morning, whether you open the passage before the feed, whether you tell the truth when a lie would be easier.

Seek first. The rest is being handled.
discussion_questions: If someone looked only at your week, what would they say is first?
What is one thing that has quietly moved into first place?
What is the smallest change that would put God's Kingdom back at the front of your day?
activity: Tomorrow morning, open Scripture before you open anything else. Notice how hard or easy that was.
